gaps.lead: I have never heard such a ridiculous excuse.
gaps.explanation: Fronted 'never' forces inversion: Never have I heard…

gaps.lead: I'm sure we went the wrong way at the last junction.
gaps.hint: must have + participle for past deduction
gaps.explanation: A deduction about the past: 'must have taken'.

gaps.lead: There isn't a single clean cup left in the cupboard.
gaps.hint: run out of = have none left
gaps.explanation: run out of = have no more of something left.

gaps.answer: can afford this holiday as long
gaps.lead: This holiday is within our price range, provided we don't go to the expensive restaurants in the tourist centre.
gaps.sentence: We ___ as we avoid the expensive restaurants in the tourist centre.
gaps.hint: provided = as long as; within our price range = can afford
gaps.explanation: 'Provided' is rewritten as 'as long as'; 'within our price range' as 'can afford'.

gaps.lead: I don't expect the company to make a profit this year, given the economic climate.
gaps.sentence: Given the economic climate, ___ the company made a profit this year.
gaps.hint: don't expect = would be surprised if + past
gaps.explanation: A tentative prediction: 'I would be surprised if + past simple'.

gaps.lead: My grandfather had completely forgotten that he phoned me last night.
gaps.sentence: My grandfather didn't ___ phoning me last night.
gaps.explanation: 'Completely forgotten' becomes 'didn't have any recollection of'.
